summary.headline: G R Infra Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 27% YoY to INR2,521 crore, but adjusted EBITDA margin fell to ~11% from 15.5%.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue grew 27% YoY to about INR2,521 crore in Q4 FY26 and 17% to INR7,620 crore for FY26, driven by oil and gas and power transmission execution. Margins compressed on higher construction costs, with standalone EBITDA margin at ~10.85% in Q4 versus 17.5% a year earlier, which included a one-time claim of INR47.5 crore. Execution slipped in March owing to a delayed appointed date on one project and geopolitical-driven fuel and bitumen price volatility, with oil and gas revenue of ~INR400-450 crore against an internal expectation of ~INR600 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of ~15% and new order wins of INR20,000-22,000 crore, while order book stands at ~INR26,470 crore.

segments.name: Roads (HAM/BOT/EPC)
segments.commentary: Transport BU order book rose ~25% during FY26; FY27 target new order book of INR12,000-14,000 crore. Management expects NHAI to tender about 6 BOT and 66 HAM projects within one to two months.

segments.name: Power transmission
segments.commentary: Focus on ~INR25,000-30,000 crore of a INR1.2 lakh crore pipeline with a FY27 order target of ~INR5,000 crore; the company is executing existing transmission projects and inventory has built up for them.

segments.name: Oil and gas pipelines
segments.commentary: Q4 execution about INR400-450 crore versus ~INR600 crore expected; FY27 revenue target INR1,000-1,200 crore, mostly from new orders; order book ~INR250 crore as of Mar-26; FY27 order target INR2,000-3,000 crore. Margin target 8-10% but not yet proven.

segments.name: Tunnel and hydro
segments.commentary: FY27 order target ~INR2,500 crore for tunnel and hydro; Agra-Gwalior BOT appointed date still awaited.

segments.name: Logistics and warehousing
segments.commentary: Plan of ~INR600-700 crore total equity over three years, with ~INR200-250 crore of equity in the current year; MMLP Indore bid awarded; dark stores in overseas markets are leased.

segments.name: Indus Infra Trust (InvIT)
segments.commentary: Sold four HAM assets for INR321 crore with exceptional gain of INR253 crore; InvIT holding valued at about INR2,400 crore per analyst question; FY27 cash flow from Indus expected at INR200-250 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at ~15%, with management saying 15-20% is possible in FY27 and ~20% in FY28 if inflows materialise.

FY27 order inflow target INR20,000-22,000 crore (roads INR12,000-14,000 crore, transmission ~INR5,000 crore, tunnel and hydro ~INR2,500 crore, oil and gas INR2,000-3,000 crore, other sectors INR1,000-2,000 crore).
FY27 capex guided at INR300-350 crore; FY28 capex expected to taper as FY27 equipment needs for tunnel and transmission are one-off.
Promoter contribution due on HAM and BOT projects INR3,486 crore, of which ~INR1,000 crore expected in FY27.
Margin outlook uncertain: management declined to commit beyond prior 10.5-11% range, citing fuel and bitumen exposure from geopolitics.
Execution rate to be assumed at current level, not expected to improve, per management on land-acquisition delays.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 inflow mainly BOT or HAM, and how big is the NHAI award pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: NHAI is more focused on BOT, but the company will bid both HAM and BOT; NHAI has an outlook of about INR6 lakh crore, with management expecting 70-80% of that, and awards spread across Q2-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth reach 20% in FY27 and 25-30% in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inflows drive next-year revenue, and it expects at least 15-20% growth in FY27 and about 20% in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will margin improve beyond the 10.5-11% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to commit, citing geopolitical fuel and bitumen exposure; margin outcome depends on how long the disruption lasts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 execution miss, particularly oil and gas?
qa_highlights.answer: Appointed-date delay on one project and March geopolitical disruption; oil and gas executed about INR400-450 crore versus about INR600 crore expected, slowed by price changes and awaited price-variation clauses.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timing for the Agra-Gwalior BOT and the two HAM appointed dates?
qa_highlights.answer: Agra-Gwalior appointed date expected around September-end after the monsoon; the two HAM appointed dates are expected October to February, subject to land availability; land status not shared on call.

qa_highlights.question: Why is execution rate falling versus order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed land aggregation: piecemeal land raises cost and slows work, and provisional appointed dates led to mobilisation before land was ready. Execution rate to be assumed at current level.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Nashik-Phata BOT bid and the MSRDC projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Nashik-Phata (about INR7,300 crore) is under NHAI evaluation as far as management knows; two MSRDC L1 projects (Pune Ring Road and Nagpur-Chandrapur) were annulled and are going to re-bid, with the Western Pune Ring Road project in progress.

capex_capacity: FY27 capex guided at INR300-350 crore, versus roughly INR100 crore a year over the prior three years; management said FY28 capex of INR300-400 crore is not currently seen, tied to one-off tunnel and transmission equipment.
Q4 FY26 fixed-asset additions about INR36 crore; FY26 additions about INR133 crore; net block of PP&E incl. WIP and intangibles about INR1,057 crore at FY26 end.
Depreciation about INR46 crore in Q4 FY26 versus INR60-65 crore at peak; management said depreciation should stay broadly flat as old equipment is recycled.
Promoter contribution: total required about INR5,400 crore, of which INR2,055 crore paid and INR3,486 crore balance; about INR1,000 crore expected in FY27.

Logistics and warehousing: about INR600-700 crore equity over three years, about INR200-250 crore in FY27; MMLP Indore bid awarded; Guwahati and Sambhajinagar sites under land discussion; 15 overseas dark stores held on lease.
Transmission focus pipeline INR25,000-30,000 crore of INR1.2 lakh crore; FY27 order target about INR5,000 crore; inventory built up for existing transmission projects.

Indus InvIT: four HAM assets sold for INR321 crore; price-to-book about 1.18-1.2x on transferred SPVs; plan to transfer at least three to four completed projects; InvIT stake about INR2,400 crore, with no plan yet to sell 50%.
demand_pricing: FY26 new order wins about INR10,700 crore; Q4 wins about INR5,500 crore (one tunnel and two HAM road projects); order book about INR26,470 crore; further bids of about INR13,500 crore yet to be opened.

FY27 order inflow target INR20,000-22,000 crore: roads INR12,000-14,000 crore, transmission about INR5,000 crore, tunnel and hydro about INR2,500 crore, oil and gas INR2,000-3,000 crore, other sectors (ropeway, telecom, renewables, BSNL OFC) INR1,000-2,000 crore.

Transport BU order book rose about 25% in FY26. NHAI indicated about INR6 lakh crore of transport awards for FY27; about 6 BOT and 66 HAM projects expected to tender within one to two months; NHAI awards expected across Q2-Q4.

Oil and gas: Q4 execution about INR400-450 crore versus about INR600 crore expected, attributed to fuel and petroleum price swings and delayed price-variation clauses. FY27 revenue target INR1,000-1,200 crore, mostly from new orders with existing clients; order book about INR250 crore at Mar-26.

Pricing: management said NHAI estimates now sit 30-40% below the estimate versus about 20% above earlier, driven by competition; cost of materials not falling in step. Fuel and bitumen account for about 30-40% of road/transport costs per management.
Growth: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 15%, with 15-20% possible and about 20% in FY28 if inflows materialise. Standalone revenue Q4 INR2,521 crore; FY26 INR7,620 crore.
risks_watch: Fuel and bitumen price volatility from the Middle East conflict: about 40% of road cost exposed, with pass-through described as incomplete in abnormal conditions.
Execution slippage: Q4 oil and gas shortfall (INR400-450 crore vs about INR600 crore) and land-acquisition delays; execution rate assumed flat.
Working capital: 128 days versus 117 days, standalone HAM debtors INR1,667 crore; consolidated operating cash flow weak.
Appointed dates still pending: Agra-Gwalior BOT (about INR3,600 crore DBFOT referenced), two HAM projects, BSNL ROW clearance expected in about one month.
Logistics and warehousing equity of INR600-700 crore over three years will weigh on ROE near term; Income Tax search from Oct-25 has show-cause notices pending.
Watch Q1 FY27: NHAI BOT/HAM tender launches, FY27 order wins against INR20,000-22,000 crore target, and any margin update on oil and gas.
key_quotes: Execution rate we have to assume at same level. I don't think it is going to increase.
It is not that construction cost is increasing; it is basically revenue which is decreasing, and where it is perceived that construction cost is increased, right?

So, margin has yet to be seen. I mean, let us complete one or two cycle on this particular sector and then only we'll be able to give you some guidance on what kind of margin which we are expecting on the sector.
Land aggregation is the biggest challenge in the sector.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on long-term infrastructure opportunities and order inflow, but cautious on margins and near-term execution, repeatedly declining to commit beyond the 10.5-11% range because of geopolitics. Answers on oil and gas margin and land-led execution were hedged, with the company saying it needs one or two cycles before guiding.

adds.what: Logistics and warehousing equity deployment (MMLP Indore bid awarded; Guwahati and Sambhajinagar sites under land discussion)
Fixed-asset/equipment additions for tunnel and transmission execution (FY27 capex INR300-350 cr)

growth.why: Management guided FY27 revenue growth of ~15% (15-20% possible) backed by a ~INR26,470 crore order book and FY27 order target of INR20,000-22,000 crore, though no new productive capacity is being added beyond FY27 capex of INR300-350 crore for equipment, and oil and gas execution slipped in Q4.
